title: Beyond Monolithic AI: A Federated Epistemic–Operational Architecture for Superadditive Cooperative Intelligence
abstract: Modern AI agents increasingly integrate perception, reasoning, planning, and action within a single monolithic architecture. Such designs can be highly capable, but they rarely provide explicit mechanisms for preserving uncertainty, governing changes to their own policies, or safely federating knowledge across agents. For safety-critical systems this is a serious gap: overconfidence, opaque decision-making, and unsafe coordination can each lead to catastrophic failure. We present the Federated Epistemic–Operational Architecture (FEOA), a constitutional design for building corrigible agents under uncertainty, and use it to introduce an architectural property we call Superadditive Cooperative Intelligence (SCI): capability that arises from governed cooperation rather than from scaling an individual model. FEOA separates agent behavior into three explicit layers — an epistemic belief substrate (Layer 1), an operational claim-acquisition layer (Layer 2), and a goal-directed action layer (Layer 3) — governed by a constitutional hierarchy in which Constitution outranks Policy, which outranks Action. Its central design principle is that cooperating agents exchange evidence rather than belief scores, which preserves each agent's local sovereignty while preventing the confidence corruption that repeated, correlated reports would otherwise cause. We validate the architecture with a dependency-free reference implementation and experiments spanning navigation and aerial-survey agents. The results show that FEOA resists false confidence under correlated-error conditions, and that heterogeneous agents cooperating across domains produce decisions that exist in no agent alone — a ground agent acting correctly on a hazard only an aerial agent could perceive. Together these results illustrate SCI: governed cooperation that makes each sovereign agent a more capable decision-maker than it could be alone — transforming the agents rather than merely pooling their outputs, and without sacrificing their sovereignty.

The results show that FEOA resists false confidence under correlated-error conditions, and that heterogeneous agents cooperating across domains produce decisions that exist in no agent alone — a ground agent acting correctly on a hazard only an aerial agent could perceive. Together these results illustrate SCI: governed cooperation that makes each sovereign agent a more capable decision-maker than it could be alone — transforming the agents rather than merely pooling their outputs, and without sacrificing their sovereignty.

title: Scaling Intermediate-Task Datasets and Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer in Multilingual Models
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does scaling the size of intermediate-task datasets (e.g., 1K vs. 100K samples) impact zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME-R benchmarks when using multilingual models fine-tuned on non-English intermediate tasks? title: Surrogate-Model-Driven SMOTE: Learning to Generate Data via Adaptive Boundary-Aware Optimization
abstract: Class-imbalance is a pervasive and challenging issue in machine learning, where traditional classifiers often exhibit a strong bias towards the majority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants mitigate this problem by interpolating between minority instances, their reliance on local geometric distances often introduces noisy samples into the majority class regions, leading to severe class overlapping and over-fitting. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Surrogate-model SMOTE (SM-SMOTE), which introduces an efficient, differentiable surrogate model specifically trained to learn "how to generate high-quality data." Instead of performing blind random interpolation, SM-SMOTE leverages the surrogate model to perceive the global decision boundary and adaptively guide the sample generation process. We formulate the synthesis of new samples as a joint optimization problem that maximizes minority class confidence, captures boundary uncertainty, and applies regularization to preserve the original data manifold. By utilizing gradient flow directions, the initial candidate points are iteratively adjusted to find the optimal positions that expand the minority decision space without invading the majority class domain. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that SM-SMOTE effectively balances exploration and exploitation during data synthesis, substantially reducing negative transfer while enhancing the classifier's discriminative capability along complex boundaries.

title: Active Reset and Scheduling in Fault-Tolerant Quantum-Classical Cloud Computing
abstract: Quantum-classical cloud computing refers to a hybrid computing model that integrates quantum computing with classical computing resources, typically hosted on the cloud. The objective of this paper is threefold: First, to scrutinize the computing paradigm of quantum-classical cloud computing; second, to study the three pillars of the underpinning techniques: Active reset, scheduling, and fault tolerance; third, to demonstrate the realization of the aforementioned techniques. The active reset method leverages measurement and feedback to reset the qubit much faster and with high fidelity. The proposed scheduling algorithm is designed to efficiently manage quantum job execution in a fault-tolerant quantum-classical cloud computing environment. The paper also implements a Bayesian optimization process to optimize the hyper-parameters of a quantum error correction scheme. The research demonstrates significant performance gains across all three technical pillars of the hybrid cloud model. Specifically, the implementation of active reset reduced the qubit initialization time by 90 %, dropping from the 100 µs required for passive relaxation to just 10 µs while maintaining a high reset fidelity of 99.6 %. In terms of cloud resource management, the Shortest Job Next (SJN) scheduling algorithm drastically improved efficiency compared to FCFS, reducing peak wait times from 1.75 s to near-zero for many tasks. Furthermore, the application of Bayesian optimization to faulttolerant parameters successfully minimized the logical error rate from an initial 0.238 to 0.106, marking a 55 % improvement in the reliability of the quantum-classical computing environment.

title: Adopción e integración de inteligencia artificial en el proceso gerencial de toma de decisiones: un estudio exploratorio en empresas de servicios tecnológicos argentinas
abstract: La adopción de Inteligencia Artificial ha experimentado una aceleración sin precedentes desde 2022, pero persiste una brecha significativa entre el potencial tecnológico y el valor organizacional efectivamente capturado. Este estudio analiza la adopción e integración de herramientas de IA en los procesos gerenciales de toma de decisiones en empresas del sector de servicios tecnológicos en Argentina, explorando las percepciones directivas sobre los desafíos y oportunidades que presenta este fenómeno. La investigación adopta un diseño metodológico mixto que combina datos cuantitativos de 26 organizaciones mediante cuestionario estructurado con hallazgos cualitativos de seis entrevistas semiestructuradas con líderes empresariales. El análisis se estructura mediante un marco conceptual de cuatro niveles que examina el contexto sectorial, los factores organizativos, los procesos de adopción y los resultados capturados. Los hallazgos revelan que el sector se encuentra en una fase de adopción amplia pero predominantemente superficial. El 73% de las organizaciones utiliza herramientas de IA, con predominio de asistentes generativos (94.7% de usuarios), pero la integración permanece mayormente instrumental-táctica más que estratégica-transformadora. La penetración de IA es significativamente mayor en decisiones operativas que en estratégicas, con solo el 26% de los encuestados percibiendo mejoras en la objetividad de las decisiones. Los beneficios más reportados se concentran en eficiencia operativa: velocidad de análisis (73%), automatización de tareas (69%) e identificación de patrones (58%). El estudio confirma la primacía de factores organizacionales sobre limitaciones técnicas como determinantes del éxito: el 65% identifica falta de conocimiento técnico como barrera principal, el 54% problemas de calidad de datos, y el 46% dificultades de integración con sistemas existentes. Las estructuras de gobernanza permanecen mayormente informales, con solo el 23% de organizaciones reportando políticas formales de uso de IA. Los hallazgos sugieren que la adopción efectiva constituye fundamentalmente un desafío de gestión del cambio más que un desafío técnico.

title: Decorrelated unbiased converted measurement Kalman filter for bistatic radar
abstract: Bistatic position measurements in radar systems are nonlinear functions of the Cartesian state. These nonlinearities pose challenges for many target tracking algorithms, leading to the well-known 'contact lens' effect, manifesting as nonlinear measurement artifacts in Cartesian coordinates. In monostatic radar, the CMKF (converted measurement Kalman filter) is commonly used to mitigate nonlinearities in measurements. However, the converted measurement model for bistatic radar lacks a closed-form expression, motivating our research to address this challenge. A track initiation technique for bistatic radar is developed, and the initial state is propagated and incorporated into the DUCM (decorrelated unbiased converted measurement) framework to reduce model complexity. The filter parameters of the proposed DUCM model parameters are derived through theoretical analysis, and the filtering steps are described. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to other classical techniques.

title: Comprehensive guidelines for establishing sample diversity and data sufficiency in artificial intelligence diagnostic datasets for cervical liquid-based cytology
abstract: Liquid-based cytology (LBC) has become a core technology in cervical cancer screening, and artificial intelligence (AI) shows great potential in addressing issues such as the global shortage of cytopathologists and large variations in diagnostic results. However, the clinical reliability of AI systems in the field of cervical cytology fundamentally depends on the quality, diversity, and representativeness of their training and validation datasets. Drawing on evidence-based medicine principles, the latest research progress in China and globally, and clinical practices, these guidelines establish standardized requirements for sample diversity and data sufficiency in cervical LBC AI datasets to reduce algorithmic bias. The objective is to improve the real-world applicability of models and ensure their safe clinical application. This guideline strictly complies with standardized guideline development specifications, with transparent expert panel organization, systematic literature retrieval, standardized evidence grading, three-round Delphi expert consensus, external peer review, and dynamic update mechanisms. All quantitative threshold indicators in the recommendations are jointly formulated based on high-quality clinical evidence and expert consensus, with clear evidence sources and consensus construction processes to enhance the transparency, credibility, and operability of the guideline.

title: Quantum machine learning for object detection and segmentation: A comprehensive survey and future research directions
abstract: Small objects have become increasingly common in civil, industrial, and security sensitive environments, driving a strong demand for reliable vision-based detection and segmentation. While deep learning (DL) models have achieved impressive performance, their practicality is limited by the small sizes of objects, cluttered backgrounds, motion blur, domain shift, and the growing cost of training and inference. Quantum machine learning (QML) has recently emerged as a potential research direction for exploring alternative feature representations, optimization strategies, and learning paradigms under resource constrained conditions. However, its practical efficiency benefits for object detection and segmentation remain largely preliminary and context dependent. The literature on quantum methods for detection and segmentation is scattered across the QML, aerial vision, and remote sensing domains. We provide a structured review of quantum, hybrid quantum–classical (HQC), and quantum approaches for detection and segmentation. We classify existing methods based on four aspects: how features are encoded and represented in quantum systems, the use of quantum kernels, variational quantum circuits (VQC) for classification and detection, and quantum architectures combined with modern detection and segmentation models. We summarize the commonly used datasets for quantum techniques, evaluation protocols, and computational constraints, comparing the reported performance trends, scalability levels, and practical limitations of quantum-based methods. Finally, we identify the open challenges, including data-efficient learning, robustness to domain shift, and end-to-end quantum segmentation, along with the research directions relevant to bridging the gap between QML and real-world object perception systems.

title: Native Multi-Dimensional Subquadratic Operators via Input Dependent Long Convolutions
abstract: Subquadratic alternatives to attention require compromises when applied to multi-dimensional data: standard convolutions lack global receptive fields and input dependency, while recurrent models require rasterizing data such as images, volumes, and partial differential equation (PDE) into an ad-hoc $1\rm D$ scan order that violates their spatial structure. We introduce \textit{HyenaND}, a subquadratic, global, input-dependent operator that acts directly on the native geometry of multidimensional data through convolutions with implicitly parametrized global, input-dependent multi-dimensional convolutional kernels. Our CUDA implementation, \texttt{nSubQ}, fuses the FFT-convolution path to turn HyenaND's $\mathcal{O}(L \log L)$ scaling into wall-clock speedups. Across long-context genomics, computer vision, medical imaging, and PDE modeling, pure HyenaND stacks match the accuracy of strong attention baselines, while hybrid configurations that interleave HyenaND and attention layers outperform both pure attention and strong recurrence-based hybrids.

title: BrainFIBRE: A Foundation Model via Information Decomposition for Brain Microstructure
abstract: Diffusion MRI probes brain microstructure with particular sensitivity to early cerebrovascular and neurodegenerative changes. Neurite Orientation Dispersion and Density Imaging (NODDI) decomposes the diffusion signal into three biophysically interpretable maps: neurite density index (NDI), orientation dispersion index (ODI), and free water fraction (FWF), capturing neurite packing, fiber coherence, and extracellular fluid. These 3D maps offer a rich substrate for transferable microstructural representations, yet integrating them is challenging: standard representation learning struggles to disentangle the unique information in each map from their shared and synergistic interactions. We present BrainFIBRE, the first foundation model for brain microstructure, pretrained on NODDI-derived maps from 55,592 UK Biobank participants. We propose Self-supervised Partial Information Decomposition (SPID), which extends PID-guided multimodal learning to the self-supervised regime for the first time. A novel Counterfactual Candidate Construction (CCC) paradigm perturbs inter-modality alignment through modality dropping and swapping, providing the contrastive signal for a Mixture-of-Experts architecture to disentangle unique, synergistic, and redundant information without any downstream label. On both Caucasian and Asian cohorts, BrainFIBRE achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks predicting age, sex, cerebrovascular and neurodegenerative markers, and cognition, while yielding neurobiologically interpretable representations that reveal task- and cohort-specific interaction patterns. BrainFIBRE establishes a versatile foundation for neuroimaging analysis at the microstructural level.

A novel Counterfactual Candidate Construction (CCC) paradigm perturbs inter-modality alignment through modality dropping and swapping, providing the contrastive signal for a Mixture-of-Experts architecture to disentangle unique, synergistic, and redundant information without any downstream label. On both Caucasian and Asian cohorts, BrainFIBRE achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks predicting age, sex, cerebrovascular and neurodegenerative markers, and cognition, while yielding neurobiologically interpretable representations that reveal task- and cohort-specific interaction patterns. BrainFIBRE establishes a versatile foundation for neuroimaging analysis at the microstructural level.

title: Active Learning for Calibrating Entangling Gates via Surrogate-Based Optimization
abstract: The fidelity of a quantum gate is sensitive to small deviations in the physical control parameters. Unfortunately, it is generally difficult to exactly model the implemented Hamiltonian for a set of user-defined parameters, necessitating on-device calibration. Here, we present an active learning framework based on Bayesian optimization with a Gaussian Process surrogate to find the optimal parameter set. We validate the technique through numerical calibration of the laser amplitude and frequencies that implement the trapped-ion Mølmer Sørensen gate. We show that a Gaussian process can model the Hamiltonian dynamics. The addition of active learning accelerates the discovery of the optimal parameter set with speed and final fidelity dependent on the quantum projection noise of the data. These results establish the utility of active learning and surrogate models for quantum calibration and control.

title: The Shape of Math To Come

title: Diseño e implementación de una secretaría digital basada en inteligencia artificial para la gestión automatizada de agendas y reuniones mediante interfaces conversacionales e integración con servicios en la nube
abstract: Este trabajo presenta el diseño e implementación de una secretaria digital basada en inteligencia artificial para automatizar la coordinación de reuniones entre estudiantes, docentes y personal administrativo de la Universidad Politécnica Salesiana, sede Cuenca, a través de WhatsApp. El sistema se desarrolló siguiendo Design-Based Research (DBR) combinado con SCRUM, sobre un backend en Python (FastAPI) que conecta WhatsApp mediante WAHA con Dify, plataforma que interpreta el lenguaje natural del usuario y orquesta las acciones del sistema. La lógica de disponibilidad, la negociación de horarios y la persistencia de la información se manejan en el backend, con los datos almacenados en Supabase; al confirmarse una reunión, el sistema crea automáticamente el evento en Google Calendar y genera un enlace de videollamada en Jitsi Meet.

title: Implementación de la metaheurística Nuclear Chain Reaction y evaluación en problemas reales de ingeniería
abstract: La optimización es esencial para resolver problemas reales en los que se deben minimizar ciertas magnitudes cumpliendo restricciones. Sin embargo, la presencia de funciones no lineales, variables diversas y regiones factibles complejas dificulta el uso de métodos exactos, especialmente en espacios de búsqueda amplios. En este contexto, las metaheurísticas se han consolidado como una alternativa flexible para abordar problemas de optimización complejos. Aunque no garantizan necesariamente la obtención del óptimo global, permiten encontrar soluciones de buena calidad en tiempos computacionales razonables. Su principal ventaja es que pueden aplicarse a problemas muy diversos sin requerir una formulación matemática especialmente restrictiva. Por ello, resultan adecuadas para problemas reales de ingeniería, donde las restricciones y las características del diseño suelen tener un papel tan importante como la propia función objetivo. Este Trabajo Fin de Máster se centra en el estudio, implementación y evaluación de la metaheurística Nuclear Chain Reaction (NCR)[1], un algoritmo poblacional inspirado en el proceso de las reacciones nucleares en cadena. En NCR, cada solución candidata se interpreta como un núcleo situado dentro de un reactor, mientras que las nuevas soluciones generadas durante la búsqueda se asocian con los impactos producidos por los neutrones liberados en una fisión. El objetivo principal del trabajo es ampliar la evaluación de NCR más allá de funciones matemáticas no restringidas, aplicándola a problemas reales de ingeniería con restricciones. Para ello, se desarrolla una implementación del algoritmo y se adapta su funcionamiento a un conjunto de doce problemas benchmark ampliamente utilizados en la literatura. Entre ellos se incluyen problemas como Speed Reducer, Tension-Compression Spring, Pressure Vessel, Welded Beam, Three-Bar Truss, Multiple Disk Clutch Brake, Cantilever Beam, Himmelblau, Tubular Column, Piston Lever, Robot Gripper y Corrugated Bulkhead. Estos benchmarks permiten analizar el comportamiento de NCR en escenarios más exigentes que las funciones sintéticas, ya que incorporan restricciones no lineales, límites sobre las variables y, en algunos casos, variables enteras o discretas. Una de las principales aportaciones del trabajo es la adaptación de NCR al tratamiento de problemas restringidos. Para ello, se emplea un criterio de ranking con factibilidad. En lugar de comparar las soluciones únicamente mediante una función objetivo penalizada, el algoritmo prioriza explícitamente las soluciones factibles frente a las no factibles. Entre dos soluciones factibles, se considera mejor aquella con menor valor de la función objetivo original. Si una solución es factible y otra no lo es, se selecciona siempre la factible. Finalmente, si ambas soluciones son no factibles, se prefiere aquella con menor violación total de restricciones. Este criterio permite guiar la búsqueda hacia la región factible y evita que soluciones con buenos valores objetivos, pero inviables desde el punto de vista del diseño, dominen el proceso de selección. Además, se incorpora un tratamiento específico para variables enteras o discretas en aquellos problemas que lo requieren. En particular, se aplica reparación al número de dientes en el problema Speed Reducer, al número de espiras activas en TensionCompression Spring, a los espesores discretizados en Pressure Vessel y al número de superficies de fricción en Multiple Disk Clutch Brake. Este procedimiento consiste en redondear las variables enteras al valor permitido más cercano o, en el caso de variables discretizadas con un paso fijo, al múltiplo admisible más próximo. Otra parte relevante del trabajo es la selección de parámetros de NCR. Dado que el rendimiento de una metaheurística puede depender de forma notable de su configuración, se realiza una fase previa de ajuste para cada problema benchmark. Entre los parámetros considerados se encuentran el tamaño de población, el número de impactos generados por cada núcleo, la tasa de elitismo, el radio relativo de vecindad y las probabilidades mínima y máxima de impacto cercano. En la implementación final, el parámetro α de la formulación original se sustituye por una formulación más interpretable basada en pm´ın y pm´ax, que controlan directamente el intervalo de probabilidad de aplicar búsqueda local. El protocolo experimental se mantiene fijo en aspectos como el número máximo de evaluaciones, el número de ejecuciones independientes, las semillas utilizadas y el criterio de parada, con el objetivo de garantizar la reproducibilidad y la comparabilidad de los resultados. Los resultados obtenidos por NCR se analizan mediante métricas como el mejor valor, la media, el peor valor y la desviación típica de las ejecuciones independientes. Además, se considera también la factibilidad de las soluciones obtenidas, ya que no basta con alcanzar valores bajos de la función objetivo sino que se deben satisfacer las restricciones del problema. Los resultados se comparan de forma indirecta con los publicados en la literatura para otras metaheurísticas aplicadas a los mismos problemas. Esta comparación permite situar el comportamiento de NCR dentro de un marco experimental más amplio, aunque debe interpretarse con cautela, puesto que los algoritmos de referencia no se reimplementan bajo un mismo entorno ni el mismo tratamiento de restricciones. Los resultados muestran que NCR obtiene soluciones factibles en todos los problemas probados, lo que demuestra que el tratamiento de restricciones mediante ranking con factibilidad permite guiar la búsqueda hacia regiones válidas del espacio de soluciones. Sin embargo, el rendimiento del algoritmo no es homogéneo en todos los benchmarks. NCR presenta un comportamiento competitivo o razonable en problemas como Three-Bar Truss, Tubular Column, Pressure Vessel y Multiple Disk Clutch Brake, donde obtiene soluciones cercanas a los mejores valores publicados. Por otro lado, muestra mayores dificultades en problemas como Himmelblau, Cantilever Beam, Piston Lever y Corrugated Bulkhead, donde queda más alejado de los métodos de referencia o presenta mayor variabilidad entre ejecuciones. Finalmente, se plantean posibles líneas de trabajo futuro, entre las que destacan la incorporación de mecanismos de reparación de variables más avanzados, estrategias adaptativas de selección de parámetros y comparaciones experimentales directas con otras metaheurísticas. --ABSTRACT-- Optimization is essential for solving real-world problems in which certain quantities must be minimized while satisfying a set of constraints. However, the presence of nonlinear functions, diverse variables and complex feasible regions makes the use of exact methods difficult, especially in large search spaces. In this context, metaheuristics have become a flexible alternative for addressing complex optimization problems. Although they do not necessarily guarantee the attainment of the global optimum, they are able to find good-quality solutions within reasonable computational times. Their main advantage is that they can be applied to a wide variety of problems without requiring a particularly restrictive mathematical formulation. For this reason, they are suitable for real-world engineering problems, where constraints and design characteristics often play a role as important as the objective function itself. This Master’s Thesis focuses on the study, implementation and evaluation of the Nuclear Chain Reaction (NCR) metaheuristic [1], a population-based algorithm inspired by the process of nuclear chain reactions. In NCR, each candidate solution is interpreted as a nucleus located inside a reactor, while the new solutions generated during the search are associated with the impacts produced by the neutrons released in a fission process. The main objective of this work is to extend the evaluation of NCR beyond unconstrained mathematical functions by applying it to real-world engineering problems with constraints. To this end, an implementation of the algorithm is developed and adapted to a set of twelve benchmark problems widely used in the literature. These include problems such as Speed Reducer, Tension-Compression Spring, Pressure Vessel, Welded Beam, Three-Bar Truss, Multiple Disk Clutch Brake, Cantilever Beam, Himmelblau, Tubular Column, Piston Lever, Robot Gripper and Corrugated Bulkhead. These benchmarks allow the behavior of NCR to be analyzed in more demanding scenarios than synthetic functions, since they incorporate nonlinear constraints, bounds on the variables and, in some cases, integer or discrete variables. One of the main contributions of this work is the adaptation of NCR to the handling of constrained problems. For this purpose, a feasibility-based ranking criterion is used. Instead of comparing solutions solely by means of a penalized objective function, the algorithm explicitly prioritizes feasible solutions over infeasible ones. Between two feasible solutions, the one with the lower value of the original objective function is considered better. If one solution is feasible and the other is not, the feasible solution is always selected. Finally, if both solutions are infeasible, the one with the lower total constraint violation is preferred. This criterion helps guide the search towards the feasible region and prevents solutions with good objective values, but infeasible from a design perspective, from dominating the selection process. In particular, repair is applied to the number of teeth in the Speed Reducer problem, to the number of active coils in Tension-Compression Spring, to the discretized thicknesses in Pressure Vessel, and to the number of friction surfaces in Multiple Disk Clutch Brake. title: On the consolidation of knowledge in large language models
abstract: Les grands modèles de langage (LLMs) sont rapidement devenus une technologie centrale de l’intelligence artificielle, démontrant des capacités remarquables dans un large éventail de tâches linguistiques et de raisonnement. Pourtant, malgré leur fluidité et leur polyvalence, ces systèmes présentent encore des limites dans la manière dont ils acquièrent et organisent les connaissances. Ils peuvent mémoriser un grand nombre de faits, mais échouent parfois à les intégrer dans des modèles du monde cohérents et consistants. Cette thèse examine l’une de ces limites — le problème de la consolidation des connaissances — et soutient qu’elle constitue un obstacle fondamental à une compréhension plus profonde et à une fiabilité accrue des modèles de langage à grande échelle. La consolidation des connaissances désigne le processus d’intégration d’informations distinctes, de résolution des contradictions et d’inférence des relations implicites afin que le savoir devienne internement cohérent et interconnecté. Alors que les humains consolident naturellement leurs connaissances par le raisonnement, la réflexion et l’abstraction, les LLMs, entraînés par la prédiction du prochain jeton, manquent de mécanisme favorisant explicitement ce processus. Ils apprennent à prédire les jetons dans des contextes locaux, mais ne reçoivent pas systématiquement de signal d’apprentissage pour intégrer des informations s’étendant à travers différents documents, périodes ou sujets. En conséquence, leurs représentations internes peuvent rester fragmentées : ils peuvent stocker des faits contradictoires, négliger des implications implicites ou échouer à raisonner de manière cohérente sur des informations distribuées. Cette thèse propose à la fois un cadre conceptuel et des preuves empiriques pour comprendre cette limitation. Le chapitre 1 définit la consolidation des connaissances et la distingue de domaines connexes tels que le raisonnement multi-étapes, l’apprentissage continu et la modélisation de longs contextes. Le chapitre 2 établit les bases théoriques, en expliquant comment les objectifs d’entraînement et les architectures actuels donnent naissance à des représentations fragmentées. Les chapitres 3 à 5 présentent trois études complémentaires. La première montre comment la segmentation des documents lors de l’entraînement et de l’inférence nuit à la mémoire et au raisonnement. La seconde démontre qu’à une échelle suffisante, les modèles commencent à manifester une capacité émergente à estimer la complétude de leurs propres connaissances sur certains sujets — compensant partiellement l’absence de consolidation. La troisième révèle que des modifications structurelles des données, notamment le « document packing », peuvent localement améliorer la mémoire et la précision factuelle, sans toutefois résoudre le problème sous-jacent. Dans l’ensemble, ces résultats suggèrent que l’absence de consolidation des connaissances constitue une limite fondamentale des LLMs actuels, plutôt qu’un simple artefact des données d’entraînement ou de l’échelle. La thèse conclut en proposant des orientations de recherche pour permettre la consolidation pendant et après l’entraînement, ainsi qu’en décrivant des cadres d’évaluation pour la mesurer. Relever ce défi sera crucial pour développer des modèles qui ne se contentent pas de stocker des informations, mais qui puissent les intégrer et raisonner dessus de manière cohérente.

Les chapitres 3 à 5 présentent trois études complémentaires. La première montre comment la segmentation des documents lors de l’entraînement et de l’inférence nuit à la mémoire et au raisonnement. La seconde démontre qu’à une échelle suffisante, les modèles commencent à manifester une capacité émergente à estimer la complétude de leurs propres connaissances sur certains sujets — compensant partiellement l’absence de consolidation. La troisième révèle que des modifications structurelles des données, notamment le « document packing », peuvent localement améliorer la mémoire et la précision factuelle, sans toutefois résoudre le problème sous-jacent. Dans l’ensemble, ces résultats suggèrent que l’absence de consolidation des connaissances constitue une limite fondamentale des LLMs actuels, plutôt qu’un simple artefact des données d’entraînement ou de l’échelle. La thèse conclut en proposant des orientations de recherche pour permettre la consolidation pendant et après l’entraînement, ainsi qu’en décrivant des cadres d’évaluation pour la mesurer. Relever ce défi sera crucial pour développer des modèles qui ne se contentent pas de stocker des informations, mais qui puissent les intégrer et raisonner dessus de manière cohérente.

title: TÁC PHẨM CÓ SỬ DỤNG TRÍ TUỆ NHÂN TẠO VÀ TRÁCH NHIỆM PHÁP LÝ TRONG QUÁ TRÌNH TẠO LẬP, KHAI THÁC TÁC PHẨM
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, has transformed the creation and exploitation of works while posing significant challenges to copyright law. Key issues include the copyright protection of AI-assisted works, determining the extent of AI involvement in the creative process, and allocating legal liability in cases of infringement or disputes. This article divides the lifecycle of AI-assisted works into three stages—input, generation, and output—to examine the legal issues arising at each stage. It further proposes a framework for allocating responsibility among relevant stakeholders based on their degree of control, level of initiative, and ability to foresee and manage legal risks.

title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN PUBLIK TERHADAP PEMBANGUNAN IBU KOTA NUSANTARA (IKN) DENGAN MENGGUNAKAN METODE LONG SHORT-TERM MEMORY (LSTM)
abstract: Pembangunan Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN) sebagai proyek strategis nasional menimbulkan berbagai respon di masyarakat, baik dukungan maupun penolakan, yang dipengaruhi oleh aspek ekonomi, lingkungan, dan kebijakan pemerintah. Perbedaan pandangan tersebut menjadikan analisis sentimen penting untuk memahami kecenderungan opini publik secara sistematis. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) dengan tahapan CRISP-DM. Data diperoleh dari media sosial dan portal berita, kemudian diproses melalui tahap preprocessing sebelum dilakukan pemodelan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sentimen negatif mendominasi sebesar 52,2%, diikuti positif 28,8% dan netral 18,9%, dengan akurasi model sebesar 78,59%. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa metode LSTM cukup efektif dalam menganalisis sentimen teks berbahasa Indonesia.

title: Unravelling Employee AI Awareness (AIA): A Review, Conceptual Framework and Future Research Agenda
abstract: Employee awareness of artificial intelligence (AIA) has gained prominence in service research as scholars seek to understand how employees make sense of AI and emotionally respond to its presence in their work environments. However, prior research on AIA is scattered across disciplines and lacks conceptual coherence. Addressing this shortcoming, the present study undertakes a systematic review of the literature to bring structure and clarity to the field and to develop a coherent, process-oriented framework. Drawing on a rigorous five-stage search and screening procedure, 78 peer-reviewed articles were identified and examined using the TCCM framework to integrate insights across theories, contexts, constructs, and methods. The synthesis suggests that AIA is triggered by contextual and organizational signals, shaped through intertwined cognitive and affective processes, and gives rise to varied employee responses, depending on the resources available to individuals and organizations. In addition to advancing theory, the review provides practical guidance for service firms regarding leadership approaches, workforce planning, capability building, and the design of supportive interventions in AI-enabled work settings, while outlining a clear agenda for future research.

title: The Ising perceptron at nonzero margin: certified bounds along the capacity curve
abstract: The storage capacity of the Ising perceptron at margin κ is predicted by a replica-symmetric variational problem whose zero-margin instance, the Krauth–Mézard constant α⋆ ≈ 0.833, was recently settled: Ding and Sun proved the lower bound, Huang proved the upper bound at general margin conditionally on four numerical hypotheses, and the zero-margin instances of those hypotheses have been verified in interval arithmetic. This paper moves the verified upper bound off the point κ = 0. Two elementary identities make the general-margin system as tractable as the zero-margin one: the replica-symmetric free energy is stationary in both order parameters exactly at the fixed point, so on each certified branch rectangle the threshold α⋆(κ) is the unique root of a strictly decreasing function; and ∂R/∂q collapses to a one-term integral with positive integrand, a form of the general-margin monotonicity of Ding and Sun that interval arithmetic can consume directly. Building on these we verify, in ball arithmetic over sub-slabs of the margin axis, Huang's fixed-point, AMP, and local-concavity conditions on the strip κ ∈ [−0.65,0.19] (1680 contiguous slabs across two uniqueness lanes, the second carrying per-slab thin-rectangle contractions and, independently, Nakajima's saddle theorem under a certified premise), with α⋆(κ) located to width 2 ⋅ 10−6 at five margins and the local maximality of the first-moment functional at its degenerate maximizer certified at six. The remaining hypothesis, the global nonpositivity of Huang's two-variable rate function, we verify at all five margins by porting the zero-margin certificate architecture to located parameter boxes: the maximizer is kept symbolic through the base-point identity ∇Φ(1,0) = (ψ0(1−q0),q0), the dual localization is evaluated through a correlated Bregman integrand that collapses algebraically, and the far-tail kernels are stabilized by classical Mills-ratio bounds. At each of the five margins all four hypotheses hold, so Huang's theorem gives unconditional capacity upper bounds, for instance α⋆(0.05) ∈ [0.781073068,0.781074776] and α⋆(−0.45) ∈ [1.557652103,1.557654133]. The verification code, certificates, and replay instructions are at https://github.com/yspennstate/ising-perceptron-margin. On the lower-bound side, open at every nonzero margin, we prove that unconditioned second moments fail at every margin (with a closure over nonnegative weights for κ ≥ 0), derive capacity lower bounds for all κ < 0 by embedding a symmetric perceptron, and verify in floating point that the general-margin form of Ding–Sun's lower-bound condition holds at all five certified margins.

title: Reproducibility archive for: How Fast, How Sure, and Where It Breaks: A Streaming Sequential-Decision Layer for Voice-Deepfake Detection under Real Telephony Codecs
abstract: Reproducibility archive for the paper "How Fast, How Sure, and Where It Breaks: A Streaming Sequential-Decision Layer for Voice-Deepfake Detection under Real Telephony Codecs." This archive contains the source code and experimental result artifacts needed to reproduce the paper's reported numbers. It includes: the streaming sequential-decision layer, the real-codec telephony degradation pipeline (Opus, Speex-WB, EVS, AMR-WB with packet loss), the per-duration calibration and commit-when-confident stopping rule, the max-confidence selector (oracle) decomposition, the metric code, and the analysis and figure-generation scripts. The vendored AASIST backbone and its weights are included under their original MIT license; RawNet2 transfer scripts are provided. Result artifacts cover the clean-condition EER reproduction, the three-seed 21-condition codec sweep, the streaming operating curve and per-prefix analysis, the risk-coverage and tile-padding (v1/v3) decomposition, the three-seed calibration-transfer ablation, and the RawNet2 second-backbone transfer. Not included (must be obtained separately, per their own licenses): the ASVspoof 2019 LA audio corpus, and the EVS (3GPP TS 26.443) and AMR-WB (3GPP TS 26.173) reference codec binaries, which are patent/ETSI-licensed. See the README for pointers to these sources and for the environment and reproduction instructions. Original code is released under the MIT License. The vendored AASIST component retains its own MIT license.

title: МЕТОД КЕРУВАННЯ МАШИН ДЛЯ ЗЕМЛЯНИХ РОБІТ НА ОСНОВІ НЕЙРО-НЕЧІТКИХ ЕКСПЕРТНИХ СИСТЕМ
abstract: МЕТОД КЕРУВАННЯ МАШИН ДЛЯ ЗЕМЛЯНИХ РОБІТ НА ОСНОВІ НЕЙРО-НЕЧІТКИХ ЕКСПЕРТНИХ СИСТЕМ Анотація.Сьогодення потребує розвитку наукових досліджень з удосконалення існуючих та розробки нових систем автоматизованого та автоматичного керування машинами для земляних робіт.Застосування класичних методів керування у таких системах є малоефективним через їх низьку здатність до адаптації у змінних умовах експлуатації та при варіаціях параметрів стану машини, що обумовлює необхідність розробки нових підходів до автоматизації машин для земляних робіт.Низькі темпи інтелектуалізації машин для земляних робіт обумовлені відсутністю єдиного системного підходу, моделей та методів створення інтелектуальних систем керування, що враховують специфіку машин для земляних робіт.Удосконалення методів інтелектуального керування машинами для земляних робіт можливе на основі нейро-нечітких експертних систем, що підвищує швидкість формування керуючих впливів.В умовах експлуатації машин для земляних робіт виникає потреба в більш гнучкому підході, здатному враховувати різнотипні дані та самонавчатися на їхній основі.Тому доцільно поєднати нечітку логіку з адаптивною експертною системою.Таке поєднання дозволяє оперативно оброблювати різнорідну інформацію про стан машини та середовища, самонавчатися на нових даних і робити висновки в умовах невизначеності.Запропонований метод складається з двох великих процедур: пошук рішення стосовно машин для земляних робіт та пошук рішення стосовно

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Customer Satisfaction in Nepalese Banks: A Study of Karnali, Nepal
abstract: Purpose: Artificial Intelligence is transforming financial services by enabling automation, personalization, and intelligent decision-making; however, its impact on customer satisfaction in backward regions of Nepal, such as Karnali Province, remains largely unexplored. This study examines how Artificial Intelligence influences customer satisfaction, with Technology-Driven Customer Experience (TDC) serving as a mediating variable. Methods: A descriptive and causal research design is adopted to both describe the current adoption and use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled financial services and to examine the causal relationships between AI and customer satisfaction. Survey data were collected from 150 respondents who use internet banking, mobile banking, and digital payment services through a structured questionnaire. Construct reliability and validity, as well as the hypothesized relationships, were tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results: TDC is significantly positively influenced by digitalization, as shown by the path coefficients (β = 0.749, t = 12.306; β = 0.686, t = 8.487). The findings also reveal a weak but significant direct effect of digitalization on customer satisfaction (β = 0.219, t = 2.891). Furthermore, the model explains 56.1% of the variance in TDC and 74.5% of the variance in customer satisfaction, confirming the mediating role of TDC. Conclusion: Financial institutions should focus on digital skills education, user-centered innovation, and secure platforms to support service adoption and customer satisfaction in semi-urban and rural areas.

title: Truth-Tracking by Iterated Belief Change
abstract: We investigate the truth-tracking performance of iterated belief change operators. In particular, we show that a class of improvement operators is guaranteed to converge to the truth when the input sequence contains sufficiently many correct pieces of information, and we establish a corresponding convergence theorem. We also report experimental results indicating that this convergence typically occurs with relatively short input sequences.

title: Hybrid Method of Improved VAE and BiLSTM for Unsupervised Time Series Anomaly Detection
authors: ZHANG Chunhao, XIE Bin, ZHANG Jiahao
abstract: Time series anomaly detection is a critical task in the finance, medical treatment, and industrial monitoring fields. However, when handling time series data, traditional methods often face challenges such as limited feature extraction ability, poor generalization ability, and poor real-time performance. These methods may even ignore the temporal relationships between data. To fully consider the temporal dependencies in time series data and further enhance the ability to detect anomalies, this paper proposes an unsupervised time series anomaly detection method called β-VAE-BiLSTM. First, the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) network structure is customized for data reconstruction in anomaly detection. Next, a hyperparameter, β, is introduced to control the weight of the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence term in the evidence lower bound, enhancing the encoder module's disentanglement and expressive capabilities in the latent space and obtaining more robust data representations. Then, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) is used to estimate the long-term correlations of the latent representations, capturing their forward and backward dependencies and performing temporal predictions. Finally, the reconstruction error is calculated by averaging the fusion of the prediction results and the decoder reconstruction. The optimal threshold for anomaly detection is determined through grid search. Experimental results show that the proposed method has superior anomaly detection performance on multiple public time series datasets. It can effectively extract complex temporal data features, achieve efficient computation and real-time anomaly detection, identify anomalous points and regions, improve detection accuracy and robustness, and reduce false positives and false negatives.

title: SIMM-PHD filtering under a dual random-fuzzy uncertainty framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel filtering approach, the Sigma-Max Inference Interacting Multiple Model Probability Hypothesis Density (SIMM-PHD) filter, specifically designed for complex multi-target tracking scenarios involving maneuvering targets. Departing from conventional methods like the IMM-PHD that rely solely on a probabilistic framework, our approach pioneers a hybrid treatment of uncertainty. It distinctly addresses stochastic uncertainty using Random Finite Set (RFS) theory for state estimation, while leveraging possibility theory to manage the epistemic uncertainty inherent in mode inference. We provide a rigorous mathematical formulation for the filter's recursive prediction, update, and mode-selection processes within the Sigma-Max inference paradigm, which leads to a computationally tractable, closed-form solution implemented with Gaussian mixtures. Comparative simulations confirm the superiority of the proposed SIMM-PHD filter. Under demanding maneuvering conditions, it demonstrates substantial gains over the traditional IMM-PHD filter in the accuracy of both target cardinality estimation and state tracking.

title: An AI-powered diagnostic system for grading and invasion of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer via TURBT specimens: A multicenter study
abstract: Early pathological examination for grading and invasion of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) via transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) specimens is a labor-intensive, subjective, and experience-dependent task, while the poor quality of TURBT specimens and the high heterogeneity of NMIBC tumors further limit diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. This study proposed a dual-channel multi-instance learning (DCMIL) model to simultaneously integrate the grading and invasion of NMIBC, while efficiently locating minor changes in the morphology and distribution of NMIBC cells in parallel. Developed on a multicenter dataset of 1332 whole slide images (WSIs) from TURBT specimens, DCMIL demonstrated outstanding accuracy and robust performance with areas under the curve of 0.851-0.983. In the reader study, DCMIL-assisted interpretation improved the diagnostic accuracy by an average of 13.31%-18.58% for inexperienced pathologists. Overall, DCMIL holds promise as a reliable initial assessment tool of NMIBC via TURBT specimens to support clinical decision-making.

title: Sparse‐View Imaging for Lung Cancer Detection Based on Generative Adversarial Networks and Deep Learning Models
abstract: ABSTRACT Lung cancer, the largest cause of cancer deaths globally, requires effective diagnostic imaging to identify and define pulmonary abnormalities. Sparse view projections lower CT radiation but diminish image quality and make diagnosis challenging. This research introduces a comprehensive approach that systematically assesses seven sparse projection levels (10–512 views) for lung cancer detection, uniquely integrating generative adversarial networks (GANs)‐based reconstruction with diagnostic performance evaluation. In contrast to previous research, our study offers a systematic framework for generating and assessing sparse‐view datasets over the entire clinical range. Given the limited availability of sparse‐view projection datasets across clinical ranges, we systematically generated sparse‐view images at multiple levels: 10, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512 projections. Three GAN architectures, standard GAN, conditional GAN (CGAN), and Pix2Pix, were employed to reconstruct high‐quality images from degraded sparse‐view data, enhancing structural integrity and diagnostic utility. A Visual Geometry Group 16‐layer (VGG16) deep learning (DL) model evaluated the diagnostic efficacy of both generated and original sparse‐view images. Results demonstrate superior performance of the Pix2Pix model, achieving structural similarity index measure values of 79.385% and 81.265% for 10‐ and 16‐view projections, respectively. Classification performance using VGG16 yielded exceptional metrics: 98.82% accuracy, 99.18% precision, 99.18% recall, 99.18% F1‐score, and 99.86% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for 10‐view projections. This GAN‐DL integration offers a clinically viable approach for sparse‐view imaging, ensuring diagnostic reliability while minimizing radiation exposure and enhancing computational efficiency, particularly critical for cancer patients requiring reduced radiation doses.

title: A Multimodal Neuro‐Adaptive Tutoring Agent for Children's Classical Chinese Poetry Learning in VR
abstract: ABSTRACT This work offers a dual‐loop neural‐adaptive VR teaching agent to mitigate cognitive load fluctuations, enhance abstract semantic comprehension, and counteract declining motivation in children's classical Chinese poetry learning. The system amalgamates multimodal inputs, such as EEG and eye tracking, to incessantly deduce learners' cognitive states and synchronize instructional feedback across micro‐ and macro‐level loops. An inference engine based on random forests was developed, employing a heuristic pseudo‐labeling method to address label scarcity. Offline assessments validated consistent classification across various cognitive states. In the micro loop, inferred states prompt immediate task‐specific interventions; in the macro loop, they govern the rate of learning and the timing of reviews, establishing a dual‐loop system that connects momentary learning with long‐term memory organization. A controlled experiment with a between‐subjects design assessed system‐level impacts in genuine poetry learning contexts. In comparison to a nonadaptive VR baseline, the neural‐adaptive system markedly improved children's comprehension of poetic imagery and semantics, augmented memory retention, diminished perceived cognitive load, and heightened learning desire. The findings indicate that integrating real‐time cognitive state awareness with dual‐loop adaptive training provides an efficient and pragmatic framework for immersive classical poetry education in youngsters.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Systematic Literature Review of Disease Spread Models
abstract: Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have created new opportunities to streamline and potentially automate many research processes, including systematic literature reviews (SLRs). This study reports an LLM pipeline development for extracting model-relevant information from 536 peer-reviewed agent-based modeling papers. We compare the results with those of a human-conducted SLR. Our results show paper-level accuracies of approximately 77.95% for GPT-4.1 and 81.67% for GPT-5.0. Field-level accuracy ranges from 32.40% to 100.00%, with more complex or subjective fields performing less reliably. Importantly, we find that agreement between LLMs is a potential indicator of output quality: low agreement may signal hallucinations, whereas high agreement combined with low accuracy may point to noise or errors in the human dataset. Overall, our study provides practical insights into prompt development and highlights both the potential and limitations of using LLMs for full-scale SLRs in the modeling and simulation domain.

title: Polynomial equivalence of the global transverse-field Ising model and the gate model of quantum computation
abstract: The transverse-field Ising model has attracted a lot of attention in recent years, especially in the quantum simulation and quantum computation literature. This interest is driven by many platforms for analog quantum computation, which implement the transverse-field Ising model for solving optimization problems, such as quantum annealing. However, it has remained an open question whether the Ising model with a global transverse field is equivalent to the gate model of quantum computation. Here we answer this question affirmatively for the case of a non-monotonic time-dependent transverse field. Building on a recent result by Cesa and Pichler on global control of Rydberg atoms, we provide a construction that allows simulating arbitrary quantum circuits using the Ising model with global transverse field with polynomial overhead in time, qubit number, and energy scale. Although the polynomial overheads we establish here are large relative to what is feasible on real-world quantum hardware, our result motivates the development of more sophisticated methods for simulating quantum circuits using the Ising model with a global transverse field. Additionally, under the assumption that quantum computing is strictly more powerful than classical computing, our result serves as a no-go theorem for efficient classical simulation of the transverse-field Ising model with a time-dependent global transverse field. Therefore, our finding is relevant for multiple communities, from analog quantum simulation and quantum optimization on various platforms to complexity and control theory.

title: Spectroscopy Analysis with Machine Learning Regression for the Quantification of Carbon and Nitrogen Contents in Inceptisol and Oxisol Soil Types: Comparing Different Preprocessing and Validation methods as well as Feature Importance
abstract: Near-Infrared (NIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a promising alternative to traditional soil analysis methods, offering advantages such as speed, low cost, and non-destructive testing. This work proposes a machine learning (ML) approach to calibrate predictive models for carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) content in Oxisols and Inceptisols, utilizing NIR spectral data acquired with a portable MyNIR device. Various preprocessing methods were evaluated, with the most effective being the Savitzky-Golay (SG) filter and a robust outlier removal method based on the Nonlinear Iterative Partial Least Squares (NIPALS) algorithm coupled with a Huber loss function. Multiple validation strategies were compared, including 10-fold cross-validation, leave-one-out, and holdout via the Kennard-Stone method, followed by standardization. Stacking ensemble learning models were employed, using Partial Least Squares (PLS), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Ridge as base models, with linear regression as the meta-model. The models were evaluated using R2, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Ratio of Performance Deviation (RPD) metrics. The performance gap between soil types suggests the influence of pedological characteristics. Furthermore, the models achieved an RPD > 2.0 with low overfitting, validating the potential of this approach for rapid C and N quantification. This study contributes to the optimization of sustainable agricultural practices, aligning with the demand for efficient and environmentally friendly analytical methods. The developed technique enables faster decision-making for producers and consultants based on organic matter content, fertility indicators, and nutrient availability.

title: Enhancing Hotel Recommendations with AI: LLM-Based Review Summarization and Query-Driven Insights
abstract: The increasing number of data a booking platform such as Booking.com and AirBnB offers make it challenging for interested parties to browse through the available accommodations and analyze reviews in an efficient way. Efforts have been made from the booking platform providers to utilize recommender systems in an effort to enable the user to filter the results by factors such as stars, amenities, cost but most valuable insights can be provided by the unstructured text-based reviews. Going through these reviews one-by-one requires a substantial amount of time to be devoted while a respectable percentage of the reviews won't provide to the user what they are actually looking for. This research publication explores how Large Language Models (LLMs) can enhance short rental apartments recommendations by summarizing and mining key insights from user reviews. The web application presented in this paper, named "instaGuide", automates the procedure of isolating the text-based user reviews from a property on the Booking.com platform, synthesizing the summary of the reviews, and enabling the user to query specific aspects of the property in an effort to gain feedback on their personal questions/criteria. title: Structured decision-making in LLM agents using decision networks
abstract: Muchas decisiones importantes se toman bajo incertidumbre, y los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM, por sus siglas en inglés) se utilizan cada vez más para respaldarlas. Sin embargo, sus respuestas son difíciles de interpretar y verificar. Las probabilidades de los posibles resultados, el valor de cada resultado y las relaciones entre los factores relevantes suelen permanecer implícitos, lo que dificulta entender por qué se prefiere una recomendación. Como resultado, la recomendación no puede comprobarse formalmente, no está garantizado que sea óptima y puede contener errores de cálculo. El análisis de decisiones (DA, por sus siglas en inglés) aborda estos problemas mediante redes de decisión (DN, por sus siglas en inglés, también conocidas como diagramas de influencia), que hacen explícita la estructura de un problema de decisión y permiten resolverlo mediante algoritmos exactos. Su principal inconveniente es que normalmente son construidas manualmente por un analista que trabaja con un experto en el dominio. Esta tesis explora la integración de ambos enfoques como una forma de hacer más interpretable el apoyo a la toma de decisiones mediante LLM. En concreto, se proporciona al LLM un conjunto de herramientas deterministas que le permiten construir y editar de forma controlada una DN de manera iterativa, mediante llamadas específicas para crear nodos, añadir arcos o editar valores de probabilidad, entre otras operaciones. Estas herramientas forman parte de una librería especializada en la creación y edición de DN. Al obligar a representar los supuestos de la recomendación en una red explícita, el sistema combina la expresividad de los LLM con la formalidad, la verificabilidad y la interpretabilidad de las DN. La interfaz empleada para ofrecer estas herramientas al LLM es Model Context Protocol (MCP, por sus siglas en inglés), mientras que la librería utilizada para albergar la DN es PyAgrum. El código fuente completo del sistema está disponible en el repositorio de GitHub. --ABSTRACT-- Many important decisions are made under uncertainty, and large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support them. Their answers, however, are difficult to interpret and verify. The probabilities of possible outcomes, the value of each outcome, and the relationships between the relevant factors usually remain implicit, making it unclear why a recommendation is preferred. As a result, the recommendation cannot be formally checked, is not guaranteed to be optimal, and may contain calculation errors. Decision analysis (DA) addresses these issues with decision networks (DNs, also known as influence diagrams), which make the structure of a decision problem explicit, interpretable, and solvable by exact algorithms. Their main drawback is that they are usually built by hand by an analyst working with a domain expert. This thesis explores the integration of both approaches as a way to make LLMsupported decision making more interpretable. Specifically, the LLM is provided with a set of deterministic tools that allow it to build and edit a DN in a controlled and iterative way, through specific calls to create nodes, add arcs, or edit probability values, among other operations. These tools are part of a library specialised in the creation and editing of DNs. By forcing the assumptions behind the recommendation to be represented in an explicit network, the system combines the expressiveness of LLMs with the formality, verifiability, and interpretability of DNs. The interface used to provide these tools to the LLM is Model Context Protocol (MCP), while the library used to host the DN is PyAgrum. The complete source code of this system is available in the GitHub repository.

title: Disseny i desenvolupament d’una eina per experimentació amb models de reconeixement d’imatges
abstract: Aquest treball es centra en el desenvolupament d’una aplicació que permeti a l’usuari crear, gestionar i provar models simples d’Intel·ligència Artificial enfocats en el processament d’imatges. L’objectiu és fer una plataforma intuïtiva i simple que permeti als usuari amb pocs coneixements tècnic en l’àmbit no abromar-se amb la complexitat d’una model d’IA. L'aplicació ofereix la possibilitat de gestionar tant els datasets com els models creats, facilitant tot el procés, des de la càrrega de dades fins a la predicció amb nous conjunts d'imatges. Així mateix, permet provar i avaluar els models generats per garantir-ne l'eficàcia i millorar-ne el rendiment. En aquest document es detalla tot el procés de desenvolupament, començant per la selecció de tecnologies adequades fins a l'avaluació final de l’aplicació. A més, es descriuen les decisions preses al llarg del desenvolupament de l'aplicació, amb l'objectiu de justificar els criteris emprats en cada fase del projecte.

title: Robototexnika va STEM taʼlimini texnologik taʼlim darslariga joriy etish muammolari
abstract: Ushbu maqolada texnologik ta'lim darslariga robototexnika hamda STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) yondashuvini joriy etishning ilmiy-nazariy asoslari, amaliy ahamiyati va mavjud muammolari tahlil qilinadi. Tadqiqot davomida ilmiy adabiyotlarni qiyosiy tahlil qilish, pedagogik kuzatish, suhbat, loyiha metodi hamda ta'lim jarayonini monitoring qilish usullaridan foydalanildi. Robototexnika asosidagi mashg'ulotlar o'quvchilarning algoritmik tafakkuri, muammoli vaziyatlarni hal etish, ijodiy fikrlash va muhandislik kompetensiyalarini rivojlantirishga xizmat qilishi aniqlandi. Shu bilan birga, umumiy o'rta ta'lim maktablarida robototexnikani joriy etishda moddiy-texnik baza, o'qituvchilarning kasbiy tayyorgarligi, o'quv-uslubiy ta'minot hamda zamonaviy laboratoriyalar yetishmasligi asosiy to'siq bo'lib qolayotgani kuzatildi.

title: DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH FOR LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: A MULTI-LAYER HYBRID ARCHITECTURE FOR PROMPT INJECTION DETECTION
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are now embedded in many digital systems, which has exposed a new and distinctive attack surface. The most pressing threat is the prompt injection attack, in which adversarial text causes a model to ignore its developer-defined instructions, leak its hidden system prompt, or perform unintended actions. This paper proposes a layered hybrid defense gateway that combines three complementary detectors: a fast prefilter based on lexical rules, a semantic classifier that uses word-level TF-IDF features together with a multilayer perceptron, and a character-level classifier that is robust to obfuscation. Their outputs are merged by a lightweight meta-decision block based on logistic regression. In a fully reproducible experiment, the detectors are trained on clean and standard obfuscated attacks and evaluated on held-out data that additionally contains unseen, newly phrased attacks and an unseen adaptive obfuscation style. On this controlled benchmark the proposed hybrid system reaches an F1 score of 0.989 and the lowest false-positive rate among all compared systems, clearly outperforming a brittle rule-based baseline (F1 = 0.504) and every single classifier across all attack categories. An ablation study confirms that each layer covers a distinct class of attacks, empirically supporting the defense-in-depth principle.

title: NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING, SPEECH PROCESSING, AND CONVERSATIONAL AI
abstract: This chapter presents a comprehensive treatment of Natural Language Processing (NLP), Speech Processing, and Conversational Artificial Intelligence (AI), tracing the evolution of the field from rule-based symbolic methods to statistical learning and, most recently, to large-scale neural architectures built on the Transformer. The chapter surveys the foundational representations that underlie modern language technology, including tokenization, embeddings, and sequence models; core NLP tasks such as parsing, information extraction, translation, and sentiment analysis; the architecture and training paradigms of large language models (LLMs); the acoustic and linguistic pipeline of automatic speech recognition (ASR) and text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis; and the design of conversational systems ranging from task-oriented dialogue agents to open-domain and multimodal assistants. Applications in virtual assistants, healthcare, customer service, and accessibility are discussed alongside the ethical, safety, and computational challenges that accompany the deployment of these systems at scale. The chapter concludes with an outlook on emerging directions, including end-to-end speech-to-speech modelling, retrieval-augmented generation, and multimodal foundation models that unify text, speech, and vision within a single conversational interface.

title: Detection of Cyberbullying on Facebook Twitter (X) Using Bi-Directional Long Short-Term Memory and Extreme Gradient Boost Algorithms
abstract: The social networking sites have transformed digital communication but have simultaneously enabled the escalation of harmful online behaviors, particularly cyberbullying. This recurring form of digital aggression can lead to serious emotional and psychological harm, including anxiety, depression, and in severe cases, self-inflicted injury or suicidal behavior. The timely identification and prevention of cyberbullying have become an essential focus of current research. Although numerous machine learning techniques have been applied to detect abusive content, many continue to face challenges such as inefficient kernel tuning, extended training durations, and reduced predictive accuracy. To address these limitations, this study presents a hybrid deep learning architecture that integrates a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network with the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm to improve contextual awareness and classification accuracy. The proposed framework was trained and evaluated on datasets collected from Facebook and X (formerly Twitter), capturing diverse linguistic and behavioral characteristics of user interactions. Experimental results indicate that the BiLSTM–XGBoost hybrid model outperforms conventional classifiers by effectively managing context representation, adaptive learning, and class imbalance. The model achieved 97% accuracy, 95% precision, 92% recall, and an F1-score of 96%, confirming its robustness and efficiency for cyberbullying detection in dynamic social media environments. The study helps educational institutions, online platforms and legal frameworks provide insights into how to better identify cyberbullying in real-world scenarios. The study’s high recall ensures that cyberbullies are easily identified and it enhances the understanding of how combining multiple models can lead to better performance in cyberbullying detection.

title: The storage capacity of the Ising perceptron: verification of the outstanding numerical conditions
abstract: Krauth and Mézard (1989) predicted that the maximum number of storable patterns in the Ising perceptron is MN = α⋆N + o(N) for an explicit constant α⋆ ≈ 0.833. Ding and Sun proved the matching lower bound, and Huang recently proved the matching upper bound; each result is conditional on an outstanding numerical hypothesis about an explicit low-dimensional variational problem. Their global sign clauses were supported by ordinary floating-point computations; Ding–Sun's final hypothesis also contains curvature and endpoint-derivative clauses. Huang separately used rigorous interval arithmetic for the other numerical inputs, but inherited the Ding–Sun parameter rectangle and left open the main Condition 1.3—the nonpositivity, over the whole plane, of a two-variable rate function with a degenerate point and slowly approaching tails. That unbounded optimization is the reason the capacity upper bound remained conditional. We verify both outstanding conditions in full. Reparametrizing Huang's functional into the moment coordinates of the pair (X,tanhX) compresses the plane onto a compact convex body and turns the entropy term into a per-cell linear function by convex duality; certified sweeps then establish nonpositivity on the whole body away from a star-shaped region around the distinguished degenerate point. On the star itself no box enclosure can work—the tilted covariance ∇2Φ is nearly singular and its inverse loses an essential cancellation—so we certify concavity of a majorant along rays from that point, bounding the entropy Hessian by a certified majorant of 𝔼[ff⊤maxb ∈ Lsech2(b⋅f)] over sublevel-set localizations of the dual that are themselves certified by one-dimensional sweeps; no interval enclosure of the nearly singular covariance is inverted. The same machinery, in one variable, verifies the full Ding–Sun Condition 1.2, including its strict-curvature clause at the degenerate zero and its one-sided derivative clause at the singular endpoint, and we re-establish the parameter rectangle (α⋆,q⋆,ψ⋆) on which both papers rest. Together these close the stated conditional reduction for the Krauth–Mézard prediction.

title: Scaling Pretrained Model Size and Intermediate-Task Training for Zero-Shot Transfer in Low-Resource Languages
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does scaling the size of the pretrained model amplify the benefits of English intermediate-task training for zero-shot transfer on low-resource languages within the XTREME-R benchmark? title: A Survey of Sim-to-Real Transfer Methods in Robot Learning.
abstract: Robots trained entirely in simulation often fail when deployed on real hardware — a problem known as the "reality gap." In this survey, I review the major approaches researchers have developed to close that gap, from simple randomization of simulator parameters to learned domain-adaptation networks and closed-loop system identification. I organize the literature into a clear taxonomy, compare methods on practical grounds (how much real-world data they need, what kind of gap they address, and when adaptation happens), and highlight open problems the field hasn't solved yet. I argue the most promising direction is treating the reality gap as something to be continuously monitored and corrected — the idea behind adaptive digital twins — rather than a fixed problem solved once before deployment. This ties directly into my own research interest in adaptive digital twin-based reinforcement learning for autonomous robots.

title: Ethical Methods and Approaches for Implementing Explainable AI in Healthcare with Relevance to Geriatric Assistive Technologies. A scoping review protocol
abstract: Explainability is widely regarded as a key requirement for the ethically responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare. While numerous technical approaches to explainable AI have been proposed, less is known about the ethical guidance, recommendations, and frameworks that inform how explainability should be designed and implemented, particularly in AI-based active and assisted living (AAAL) systems that interact directly with older adults and other care recipients in everyday settings.This scoping review will systematically map the literature on ethical guidance, recommendations, and frameworks for implementing explainability in AI-based healthcare technologies. The review will follow an adapted Arksey and O’Malley framework and report findings in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. Electronic searches will be conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, BELIT, CINAHL, Web of Science Core Collection, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, arXiv, and medRxiv. Eligible publications include empirical, methodological, and conceptual work providing structured guidance on the ethical design or implementation of explainability in healthcare-related AI-systems. Data will be extracted independently by two reviewers and analysed using qualitative framework analysis.

title: Multilingual Intermediate-Task Training for Robust Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer in XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of multilingual intermediate-task training on robustness in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer, as evaluated by adversarial examples and domain-shifts in the XTREME-R benchmark? title: The Civilization OS Update: Agentic AI Societies, 6G, and the Transition to a Negotiation Society (English & Japanese Editions + Visual Abstract)
abstract: This record contains the English and Japanese editions of the working paper “The Civilization OS Update: Agentic AI Societies, 6G, and the Transition to a Negotiation Society.” The paper proposes Civilization OS as a five‑layer architectural model describing a civilizational transition toward a Negotiation OS, in which AI agents autonomously negotiate, coordinate, and contract across society. It integrates insights from transaction‑cost economics (Coase, 1937; Shahidi et al., 2025), AI‑agent economics (Hadfield & Koh, 2025; Rothschild et al., 2025), algorithmic collusion (Calvano et al., 2020), and 6G standardization (ITU‑R, 2023). This Zenodo record includes: English edition (primary document) Japanese edition (supplementary translation) Infographic (visual abstract) summarizing the Civilization OS architecture The purpose of this preprint is to provide a conceptual framework for interdisciplinary research on AI‑agent societies, negotiation markets, and next‑generation communication infrastructures.
